Specifically, BioBridge-XLM achieved enhancements of 0.85% in F1 score, 0.75% in AUROC, and 0.76% in AUPRC, along with a notable 3.04% decrease in the Brier score, demonstrating marked improvements in accuracy, reliability, and prediction calibration over the baseline XLM model. The source code will be made publicly available at https://github.com/jjy961228/BioBridge.
keywords: Natural language processing;code-switching;electronic medical record;emergency department;pediatric emergency department

title: Intelligent Symptom Conversations: New Frontiers in AI-Powered Preliminary Healthcare Diagnosis
authors: K. S. Charan and B. D. Surya Manikanta and V. Sathiya Suntharam and B. M. Sai
abstract: Recent advances in AI and NLP now enable conversational healthcare assistants to perform preliminary diagnoses based on users' reported symptoms. The paper presents Intelligent Symptom Conversations, which represents a systematic review and conceptual framework that follows the development of digital triage, starting with rule-based chatbots and classical machine learning models, passing through modern large language models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and multi-agent systems. These systems are critically compared in terms of their diagnostic accuracy, scalability, and interpretability, but the most persistent issues are bias, hallucination, and the threat of compromised data privacy. We conclude that the analysis of the data has revealed that LLM-based platforms have significant advantages compared to other systems in terms of flexibility and diagnostic accuracy, which are still flawed by opaque reasoning, the absence of clinical validation, and regulation inconsistency. Markedly enough, the research gaps, such as the absence of multimodal input facilities, the inability to clearly make decisions, and the neglect of indigenous medical systems, such as Ayurveda, are also brought to the fore in this review. These discoveries guide the future agenda of creating safer, interpretable and culturally accommodating AI medical aides.
keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI);Natural Language Processing (NLP);Digital triage;Rule-Based Chatbots;Large Language Models (LLMs);Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG);Machine Learning Models;Bias;Hallucination;Multi Agent Systems;Explainability;Clinical Validation;Traditional Medicine (Ayurveda)

title: Optimizing the dynamic administration regimen of prophylactic enoxaparin in critically ill patients using reinforcement learning
journal: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
authors: C. Sun and J. Li and Z. Zhang and F. Xi and X. Wang
abstract: This study aims to optimize the dynamic administration regimen of prophylactic enoxaparin in critically ill patients to reduce the risk of VTE, major bleeding, and 30-day all-cause mortality. We developed and internally and externally validated an artificial intelligence (AI) policy utilizing Double dueling deep Q network, using data from the Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV (MIMIC-IV) database (training and internal test set) and the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD, external test set). We compared the performance among the AI policy, the clinician's policy, the weight-tiered policy, and the fixed 40- mg-once-daily (QD) policy. The rationality and explainability of AI policy were investigated. In the internal test set, the AI policy achieved the highest policy value of 13.17 and the lowest estimated incidence of all outcomes of 5.53%, compared with the clinician's policy (9.81; 23.60%), the weight-tired policy (12.14; 10.72%), and the 40-mg-QD policy (12.31; 9.05%). Compared with the clinician's policy, the AI policy was associated with a decreased risk of VTE with statistical significance (OR: 0.44, 95%CI: 0.28-0.69, P<0.001). The superiority of AI policy was confirmed in the external test set. The SHAP analysis showed that sex, primary diagnosis, time to major surgery, and weight followed by vasopressor administration were the most important features contributing to AI policy. The AI policy could provide effective and clinically reasonable recommendations for the optimal dynamic frequency and dose of prophylactic enoxaparin and could potentially be applied in clinical practice after prospective evaluation.
keywords: Critical care;thromboprophylaxis;enoxaparin;reinforcement learning;Dueling Double Deep Q Network

title: Ai-Augmented Multi-Cloud Serverless Framework for Explainable Outbreak Management in Healthcare
journal: 2025 IEEE 16th Annual Ubiquitous Computing, Electronics & Mobile Communication Conference (UEMCON)
authors: V. Venkatesan and D. Barla
abstract: We present a multi-cloud, serverless deployment framework and a complementary AI pipeline for outbreak management in large healthcare networks. The framework extends an operational rules-based system deployed during COVID-19 (15,000 employees across 295 facilities) by adding portable Infrastructure-as-Code (IaC), cost-aware scaling, and healthcare-grade security. The AI pipeline integrates facility-level forecasting (LSTM), individual risk scoring (XGBoost), anomaly detection (Isolation Forest), and contact-network analytics, with explainable AI (XAI: SHAP, LIME, counterfactuals) embedded directly into clinician workflows. Evaluation on anonymized operational logs and calibrated synthetic multi-disease streams shows improvements over (i) a rules-only production baseline and (ii) a single-vendor “siloed AI” deployment: higher predictive accuracy, lower end-to-end latency, $\sim 30 \%$ lower cost per million events, and increased clinician agreement. We explicitly delineate (A) benefits from multi-cloud portability (e.g., disaster recovery, data residency, cost control) and (B) benefits from AI augmentation. Together, these yield a portable, explainable, and cost-conscious foundation for outbreak management beyond COVID-19.
keywords: AI/ML;data engineering;electronic health records;epidemic forecasting;explainable AI;graph analytics;healthcare informatics;multicloud architecture;outbreak management;serverless computing

title: Telemedicine as a Driver of Equitable Healthcare Delivery in Low-Resource and Rural Communities
journal: 2026 2nd International Conference on Big Data & Machine Learning (ICBDML)
authors: V. Roy and Swati and A. Nagpal and Y. Joshi and D. R and A. Samatha
abstract: Proposed Adaptive Multimodal Health Continuum Network (AMHC-Net) suggests an intelligent resource-based network that targets to offer trust and just medical services to underserved populations together with remote populations. The hierarchical structure of AMHC-Net is characterized by the synergistic mechanism demonstrating multi-modal sensing, adaptive edge computing, and distributed reasoning to offer continuous care provision that will persist under bandwidth and infrastructure limitations. The model combines the real-time data provided by physiological sensors, the environment and patient-provider interactions with transformer based multimodal fusion and graph attention networks respectively to infer contextualized health inference. Contingent on a Continuity Engine based on reinforcement learning, active adjustment of both communication and data prioritization is based on optimizing the maintenance of service quality under changing connectivity conditions. Furthermore, an explainable decision support layer acts as a bridge between the outputs generated by algorithms and the expertise of the clinician, for more interpretability and trust in algorithms toward automated diagnoses. The suggested system reduces the latency, streamlines the data flow, and provides the context-dependent triage, thereby tackling the discrepancy in the accessibility of care and accuracy of the diagnostic step. Access to 92% continuity efficiency with a more than 65 percent lower transmission load can be maintained in low-resource settings as shown by preliminary simulation analyses of AMHC-Net. AMHC-Net creates a paradigm shift in the future of reliable, adaptive, and inclusive digital health ecosystems, which can traversal barriers of infrastructures and socioeconomic systems and operate effectively. The suggested technique attains an overall accuracy of 94.8 percent, indicating exceptional reliability across all assessed measures.
keywords: HETM;CARDS;FSHI;CHTF;AMHC-Net

title: Towards Explainable AI in Cardiac Diagnostic: Attention-Based Interpretation of Brugada Syndrome
journal: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Learning and Optimization (ICoAILO)
authors: E. Pasero and A. Casella and V. Randazzo
abstract: Brugada Syndrome (BrS) is a genetic cardiac disorder associated with sudden cardiac death (SCD) and characterized by specific ST-segment patterns in right precordial ECG leads. Despite advances in automated electrocardiographic interpretation, conventional deep learning (DL) models remain poorly adopted in clinical settings due to their lack of transparency. In this work, it is presented an interpretable DL framework for BrS screening that leverages soft attention mechanisms to highlight diagnostically relevant ECG segments. The proposed architecture combines convolutional layers, bidirectional LSTM units, and a trainable attention module, operating on 850 ms windows centered on the S-peak. Predictions are aggregated at the lead level to reflect clinical practice. On a multi-center labeled dataset, the model achieves 93.7% window-level accuracy and 95.1% lead-level accuracy, with F1-scores of 0.95, 0.92, and 0.89 for Brugada-like, Non-Brugada, and Ambiguous classes, respectively. Attention heatmaps consistently align with ST-segment regions in true-positive Brugada cases and distinguish ambiguous from pathological inputs more robustly than threshold-based baselines. Classification errors at the lead level are reduced by over 50% compared to a legacy binary model. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of explainable AI for Brugada detection and offer a practical step toward interpretable, trust-driven ECG triage in cardiology.
keywords: brugada syndrome;neural attention;analysis;deep learning;cardiac arrhythmias;interpretable models

title: DFU-XAI: Explainable DFU Classification with Efficientnet-B3, A Grad-CAM-Enhanced Deep Learning Framework
journal: 2026 7th International Conference on Mobile Computing and Sustainable Informatics (ICMCSI)
authors: H. C and A. Nizar and A. T
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) represents a critical diabetes-related health threat that results in both extensive lower-limb amputation cases worldwide and diabetes complications. Deep learning-based diagnostic screening systems deliver impressive diagnostic results but remain clinically questionable because they lack interpretability. The research introduces an interpretable DFU detection system that combines fine-tuned EfficientNet-B3 base model with Grad-CAM for binary classification tasks. The authors conducted tests on the publicly accessible Kaggle DFU dataset and developed the system through training on image parts and conducted testing on an independent dataset. The developed model produced perfect test accuracy (97 %) paired with identical scores for precision, recall, specificity and F1 (all 97%) and an AUC score of 0.99. The research demonstrates the proposed model's superior performance over MobileNetV2 and ResNet50 base models. The model's transparency increases due to Grad-CAM visualizations which reveal medically significant ulcer locations. The DFU-XAI screening and triage framework presents users with both reliable performance and clear system interpretability.
keywords: Diabetic Foot Ulcer;EfficientNet-B3;MobileNetV2;ResNet50;Grad-CAM;Medical Image Classification

title: An Explainable Decision Support Framework for Differential Diagnosis Between Mild COVID-19 and Other Similar Influenzas
authors: K. Chadaga and S. Prabhu and N. Sampathila and R. Chadaga and S. Umakanth
abstract: It is tough to clinically differentiate between mild COVID-19 and other similar influenzas due to their comparable transmission traits and symptoms. The Real-time reverse transcriptase-polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) test is utilized regularly to diagnose severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) despite being prone to false-negative results. In recent years, intelligent support systems have been developed for patient triage and disease diagnosis. Thus, this research utilizes machine learning to diagnose COVID-19 from routine biomarkers. Twelve feature selection techniques, which include nature-inspired techniques, have been compared to extract the essential features. Multiple classifiers, including stacking, voting and deep learning, are trained to predict the patient diagnosis. The maximum accuracy obtained by the classifiers was 95% in this retrospective study. The diagnostic predictions were further interpreted using five explainable artificial intelligence methods. Biomarkers such as albumin, protein, eosinophil and total white blood cells were crucial. Thus, automated diagnostic systems can be supportive in the accurate and timely detection of COVID-19 and similar influenza infections.
keywords: Biomarkers;explainable artificial intelligence;Mild COVID-19;nature-inspired algorithms;non-COVID-19 influenza

title: AG-STDF: Anatomy-Guided ECG Spatiotemporal Dynamical Fusion for Screening Coronary Microvascular Dysfunction
authors: J. Li and Q. Sun and L. Wang and H. Zhang and J. Yang and C. Zhang and J. Pang and Y. Chen and C. Wang
abstract: Objective: Coronary slow flow (CSF), present in 1-7% of coronary angiograms, occurs in patients with angiographically normal epicardial arteries and is associated with acute coronary syndrome, representing an unmet need in coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) management. This study proposes an anatomy-guided spatiotemporal dynamical fusion (AG-STDF) framework for CSF screening. Methods: AG-STDF integrates anatomical electrophysiological territory mapping with 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) dynamics. ECG signals are decomposed into coronary territories-left anterior descending (LAD), left circumflex (LCX), and right coronary artery (RCA)—and static morphology is fused with intrinsic dynamics (derived from dynamic modeling) using joint recurrence quantification and multi-scale decomposition. Results: AG-STDF achieves an AUROC of 0.9467 $\pm$ 0.0272 for CSF detection. At the vessel level, where therapeutic decisions are made per 2024 European Society of Cardiology guidelines, AG-STDF predicts corrected thrombolysis in myocardial infarction frame counts (CTFC) with an $\text{R}^{\text{2}}$ = 0.5951 $\pm$ 0.0666 (AUROC: 0.8428). Notably, AG-STDF performs steadily in right-dominant coronary patients, with favorable results in LAD ($\text{R}^{\text{2}}$ = 0.6753) and mild fluctuations in LCX ($\text{R}^{\text{2}}$ = 0.5673) and RCA ($\text{R}^{\text{2}}$ = 0.5296) due to anatomical variations and competitive perfusion. Anatomical constraints and spatiotemporal fusion improve AUROC by 3.5% (p $< $ 0.01) and 9.47% (p $< $ 0.05). When equipped with an Intel Core i5-10500 and NVIDIA GTX 1660S, AG-STDF processes a 10-second ECG segment in 19.37 s. Conclusion: AG-STDF allows accurate, non-invasive CSF detection and vessel-level assessment in right-dominant populations. Significance: It serves as a cost-effective CMD screening tool that may reduce invasive testing and support early diagnosis.
keywords: Coronary microvascular dysfunction;deterministic learning;electrocardiogram;spatiotemporal fusion

title: Identification of COVID-19 from Other Upper Respiratory Tract Infections Using Random Undersampling and LIME-based XAI Model
journal: 2023 14th International Conference on Computing Communication and Networking Technologies (ICCCNT)
authors: M. S. Sanim and Ferdib-Al-Islam and K. M. Hasan
abstract: The urgent need for an accurate and fast diagnosis of upper respiratory tract infections (URTI) has been made clear by the COVID-19 pandemic. Machine learning algorithms have shown the potential to aid early diagnosis and appropriate patient management by distinguishing COVID-19 from other URTIs. By analyzing clinical and laboratory factors, such as symptom profiles, vital signs, and laboratory markers, machine learning algorithms can identify distinctive patterns that set COVID-19 apart from other URTIs. Healthcare workers might use such approaches to make well-informed decisions about patient triage, isolation, and treatment, which could result in improved clinical outcomes and slower disease transmission. To achieve this goal, the current work utilizes a publicly accessible dataset of symptoms and Explainable AI to extract the most significant aspects of the symptoms. The class imbalanced problem in the dataset has been eradicated by Random Under Sampling technique. In addition, classification algorithms have been used to determine the type of disease from patient’s symptoms. These algorithms included Decision Tree (DT), Random Forest (RF), Gradient Boosting (GB), Logistic Regression (LR), Naïve Bayes (NB), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Extra Tree (ET), Bagging Classifier (BG) and Stacking Classifier. The results of the proposed work indicate that the stacking ensemble model got the highest 97.31% of classification accuracy and outperformed the previous work.
keywords: COVID-19;Machine Learning;Explainable AI;Random Under Sampling;Stacking Classifier

title: AI-driven Models with Effective Feature Selection Accurately Predict ICU Admission after Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy
journal: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
authors: P. Lou and R. Manyam
abstract: Laparoscopic Cholecystectomy (LC) is widely recognized for its benefits over open cholecystectomy, such as reduced hospital stay, postoperative pain, and mortality. Despite its safety, the risk of postoperative complications, particularly those necessitating ICU admission, remains a concern. This study aims to develop AI-driven models to predict ICU admission following LC and identify key patient-specific risk factors. The study population included 1,411 patients who underwent LC at the Irvine Medical Center between 2017 and 2022. The primary outcome was ICU admission after LC. The study analyzed 51 variables comprising patient demographics, medical history, medications, lab results, and postoperative complications using ‘recursive feature elimination with cross-validation, and five AI-driven models (Random Forest, Decision Tree, Support Vector Machine, Neural Network, and Logistic Regression). Shapley additive exPlanation (SHAP) was performed to visualize and interpret the model’s performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristics (AUROC), recall, accuracy, F1 score, and Matthews Correlation Coefficient (MCC). Results demonstrated length of stay, anesthesia duration, and discharge disposition as the top risk factors impacting ICU admission after LC. The Random Forest model demonstrated the highest predictive performance with an AUROC of 0.83. This study is the first of its kind to develop and validate AI-driven models for predicting ICU admission after LC. Future research should focus on external validation and development of AI-driven clinical decision support tools to enhance postoperative risk stratification and resource management in clinical settings.
keywords: Artificial intelligence;laparoscopic cholecystectomy;ICU admission;random forest;risk prediction;Shapley additive exPlanation (SHAP)

title: Bone Fracture Detection Using Deep Learning: A Review
journal: 2026 4th International Conference on Intelligent Data Communication Technologies and Internet of Things (IDCIoT)
authors: A. Mishra and H. Verma and R. Sharma and A. Singh
abstract: Bone fracture detection is important for clinical diagnostics and emergency medicine around the world. Manual interpretation of X-rays takes a lot of time, is prone to mistakes, and relies on the availability of experts. Deep Learning (DL) has become an effective solution, showing impressive results in visual recognition tasks. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Transformer-based architectures, like Vision Transformers (ViT), have changed the game for automated feature extraction and image understanding. This review paper provides an overview of DL and Transformer applications in bone fracture detection using X-ray images. We examine recent advancements from 2018 to 2024, discussing datasets, preprocessing, model architectures, evaluation metrics, and hybrid frameworks that combine CNNs and Transformers. Comparative analyses show that hybrid models offer better contextual and spatial learning, outperforming traditional machine learning methods. Lastly, we address challenges such as data scarcity, interpretability, and computational demands. We also look at future directions that highlight explainable AI, multimodal learning, and real-time clinical applications.
keywords: Artificial Intelligence (AI);Bone Fracture Detection;Classification;Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs);Deep Learning (DL);Hybrid Models;Medical Imaging;SelfAttention;Transformer Models;Vision Transformers (ViTs)

title: AI-Driven Chatbots: Bridging the Gap between Patients and Healthcare Providers
journal: 2025 International Conference on Networks and Cryptology (NETCRYPT)
authors: R. Gupta and D. Kumar
abstract: This paper explores the theoretical framework for an AI-driven chatbot system designed to connect patients with healthcare providers. With growing demand for accessible healthcare services, AI chatbots offer a promising solution to streamline patient triage, symptom analysis, and doctor recommendations. We review relevant literature, propose a conceptual architecture with algorithmic formulations, and present a hypothetical evaluation of system performance. Although no empirical testing is conducted, our work synthesizes existing research and outlines future directions for real-world implementation.
keywords: AI Chatbot;Healthcare;Patient-Doctor Communication;Natural Language Processing;Theoretical Framework

title: CLARA NET-A Framework of Clinically-Explainable Deep Learning for Supporting Multiclass Diagnosis of Brain Tumor from Single-Modality MRI Data
journal: 2025 International Conference on Emerging Technologies in Electronics and Green Energy (ICETEG)
authors: K. N. M. Lakshmi and D. Nandan
abstract: MRI shows detailed brain structure without invasive procedures, yet gliomas, meningiomas, and pituitary adenomas can appear similar on T1-weighted axial scans. We develop a single-modality classifier that couples a ResNet branch, which extracts local textures and edges, with a Vision Transformer that models longer-range relations across the slice. To aid review, Grad-CAM heatmaps accompany each prediction, highlighting the regions that most influenced the decision and making failure cases easier to inspect. Evaluated on the Figshare benchmark, the system attains precision of $0.9812,0.8239$, and 0.9679 for meningioma, glioma, and pituitary classes, with F1-scores of $0.9474,0.8733$, and 0.9705, respectively. These results indicate that combining convolutional and transformer pathways yields accurate classification while preserving interpretability. The approach is compact, single-sequence, and compatible with routine clinical workflows, offering an explainable assistant for triage and second-read scenarios without additional contrast or sequences. Prospective validation and external datasets will be explored in future work.
keywords: Brain tumor classification;Deep neural networks;Explainable AI;Grad-CAM;Neuro-oncology;ResNet-ViT hybrid;T1-weighted MRI;Vision Transformers

title: Advanced Multi-Scale Vision Transformer With Neural Architecture Search for Thyroid Cancer Diagnosis Using Ultrasound Images
authors: D. Venugopal and M. Mesbah and A. C. Ammari and R. Al-Hmouz and A. Qureshi and B. Salam
abstract: Accurate and interpretable differentiation of abnormal and suspicious (potentially malignant) thyroid nodules in ultrasound imaging remains a critical yet challenging task, particularly in secondary healthcare settings where rapid triage is essential. Conventional deep learning models, especially convolutional neural networks, often fail to capture long-range contextual dependencies and multi-scale morphological cues (e.g., microcalcifications, irregular margins and heterogeneous echogenicity) that are vital for reliable diagnosis. To address this, we propose a novel Multi-Scale Vision Transformer with Adaptive Feature Fusion (MSViT-AFF), a unified and explainable framework that integrates hierarchical Vision Transformer (ViT) encoders, cross-scale attention, and differentiable Neural Architecture Search (NAS). Our approach automatically learns to weight diagnostically significant scales, emphasizing high-resolution features for microcalcification detection in suspicious nodules, through an end-to-end NAS-optimized fusion mechanism. Evaluated on a rigorously curated and radiologist-validated dataset of 600 thyroid ultrasound images from Sultan Qaboos University Hospital (SQUH), comprising 300 abnormal and 300 suspicious cases, MSViT-AFF achieved 96.2% accuracy, 94.8% sensitivity, 97.1% specificity, and an AUC of 0.983 [95% CI: 0.974, 0.991], exceeding all evaluated CNN and single-scale transformer baselines with statistically significant margins (all  $p \lt 0.01$ , DeLong’s test). Moreover, a Grad-CAM-based explainability layer provides pixel-level visualizations aligned with established radiological criteria, thereby enhancing clinical trust and transparency. To assess generalization, we performed a external evaluation on the public DDTI benchmark, where the SQUH-trained MSViT-AFF was tested on DDTI under the strict zero-shot protocol, the model achieved 91.0% accuracy and an AUC of 0.920, providing evidence of cross-institutional generalization. With an inference time of only 15 ms per image. These findings suggest the model could be explored for use in resource-constrained secondary care settings, subject to further validation through prospective multi-centre studies.
keywords: Vision transformer;thyroid ultrasound imaging;multi-scale fusion;attention mechanisms;deep learning;neural architecture search;explainable AI;medical image classification

title: Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM with Attention Mechanism and Ensemble Learning for Multi-Symptom Disease Prediction: A Comparative Analysis
journal: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
authors: D. Sungeetha
abstract: Proper prediction of disease based on symptomatic presentation is a major issue in medical diagnosis especially in situations where resources are limited such as in contexts where advanced diagnostic facilities are not readily available. This research will suggest a new hybrid deep learning framework, which is a combination networks to predict multiple diseases on the basis of multi-symptom patient data. The suggested model of hybrid CNN-BiLSTM got a high accuracy of 99.39% with precision of 99.46, recall of 99.39 and F1-score of 99.40. K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) recorded the highest accuracy of 99.49 percent but the proposed model performed better than the conventional ones such as Support Vector Machines (93.29 percent), logistic regression (92.28 percent), and Naive Bayes (85.37 percent). The ensemble top five algorithm did 99.39% accuracy. The deep learning hybrid technique using attention mechanism has a strong contribution to the prediction accuracy in diseases and retains the interpretability in terms of attention weights. The high performance of the model in a wide range of disease classes evidences its viability in the real-life medical application especially in the cases of initial screening and triage.
keywords: Disease Prediction;Deep Learning;CNNBiLSTM;Attention Mechanism;Ensemble Learning;Symptom Analysis;Medical Diagnosis;Clinical Decision Support;Healthcare AI

title: ASIST TBI: A Hybrid Vision Transformer and CNN Based Tool for Predicting Neurosurgical Intervention in Acute Traumatic Brain Injury
journal: 2025 IEEE 9th International Conference on Information and Communication Technology (CICT)
authors: H. Vijayakumar and V. K
abstract: We present ASIST-TBI, a Vision Transformer deep neural network model to forecast neurosurgical intervention from non-contrast head CT in acute TBI patients. It receives CT input in the form of a programmatic pipeline of voxel resampling, preprocessing, and 3D patch spatial embedding before being classified by a transformer encoder. It was trained on 2806 prior cases and validated on a held-out set of 612 subsequent cases, and ASIST-TBI performed well with 87.6% accuracy, 0.91 AUC, 88.2% sensitivity, and 86.8% specificity. On external data set, the model performed at 84.3% accuracy and AUC of 0.89. Our approach was more predictive in ability and practicable in the clinic than baseline method, aided with visualization-based interpretability with Grad-CAM. ASIST-TBI is a useful addition to computer-based triage assistance with a suitable and robust solution for enhancing decision-making for acute emergency management in neurotrauma.
keywords: Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI);Vision Transformer;Neurosurgical Intervention;Head CT Imaging;Deep Learning;Medical Decision Support;AI in Healthcare;Triage Automation

title: Plataforma Web con Machine Learning para la Detección Temprana de Anemia Infantil en Hospitales Públicos del Perú
journal: 2025 14th International Conference On Software Process Improvement (CIMPS)
authors: B. Montes and V. Parasi
abstract: Childhood anemia is a critical public health problem in Peru, exacerbated by the limited availability of laboratory diagnostics in hospitals in rural areas. This paper describes the design and validation of a lightweight web platform that predicts the severity of childhood anemia based on clinical data collected during triage and blood hemoglobin levels. The underlying model is based on XGBoost and was trained on 30,000 clinical records following the guidelines of the Ministry of Health. Input variables include age, vital signs, symptoms, and hemoglobin. The model achieved an overall accuracy of 98.4% and an F1-macro of 0.984 with the full set of variables; it maintained 98.2% accuracy when using only ten key variables. The model was integrated into a web application accessible from any browser, and functional validation was performed with 50 real-world cases, achieving 97.9% clinical accuracy, an average latency of 1.4 seconds, and a SUS score (standardized usability scale) of 84.2. The results demonstrate that the solution is accurate, fast, and suitable for healthcare facilities with limited resources, offering a tool to support the timely diagnosis of pediatric anemia.

title: AI Mobile Health Applications: Real-Time Monitoring and Support
journal: 2025 International Conference on Innovation and Intelligence for Informatics, Computing, and Technologies (3ICT)
authors: T. A. R. Sure and A. Mittal
abstract: Mobile health (mHealth) applications are increasingly incorporating artificial intelligence (AI) to enhance healthcare delivery on smartphones and tablets. This comprehensive survey examines AI-enabled mHealth across four domains: personalized health monitoring, diagnostic decision support, mental health coaching, and clinical triage. This research demonstrates that AI achieves significant improvements in predictive analytics accuracy (15–30% over traditional methods), personalized intervention effectiveness, and healthcare accessibility in underserved regions. Four detailed case studies reveal concrete impacts: an insulin dose calculator achieving 90% food recognition accuracy, skin cancer detection matching dermatologist-level performance (87% agreement), cough analysis tools detecting pediatric pneumonia with 87% accuracy, and AI triage chatbots providing clinically appropriate recommendations comparable to human physicians. Technical analysis contrasts on-device frameworks (TensorFlow Lite, Core ML) with cloud-based models, highlighting privacy–performance trade-offs. Critical challenges persist: 78% of users report privacy concerns, 23% of diagnostic systems exhibit algorithmic bias, and 68% app abandonment rates within 30 days, alongside evolving regulatory frameworks. This research identifies emerging solutions including federated learning, TinyML for edge computing, explainable AI for clinical trust, and large language model–powered conversational agents that address current limitations and enable next-generation intelligent mHealth systems.
keywords: Mobile health AI;artificial intelligence;machine learning;healthcare diagnostics

title: GraphAE: Plant-informed Graph Autoencoder for ICS Anomaly Detection with SHAP-based Explanations
journal: 2026 IEEE 5th International Conference on AI in Cybersecurity (ICAIC)
authors: V. Heydari and K. Nyarko
abstract: Network timing in industrial control systems (ICS) distorts cross-tag relationships and inflates false alarms. We propose a lightweight graph autoencoder (GraphAE) that encodes plant structure: nodes are tags and edges follow P&ID couplings, with cross-phase links up-weighted 2.5× to capture inter-stage propagation. The model is trained on normal data and scores windows by reconstruction error. On the Secure Water Treatment (SWaT) testbed (N =44), we evaluate GraphAE against a nongraph AE–LSTM and the graph-centric GDN under identical preprocessing. All methods are compared at a matched true-positive rate of 0.90 on A2 and we report AUC–ROC and false-positive rate (FPR) both overall and inside near-prop windows (a ±10-step band around positives). At this operating point, GraphAE attains AUC–ROC =0.861 versus 0.870 for AE–LSTM and 0.841 for GDN. FPR (overall) is 0.507 for GraphAE, 0.533 for AE–LSTM, and 0.689 for GDN. In near-prop regions, FPR is 0.556 for GraphAE, 0.625 for AE–LSTM, and 0.641 for GDN. SHAP analyses with a compact A1 background (2,048 samples) highlight the tags driving high scores and support operator triage. These results show that modeling inter-signal structure reduces false alarms in networking-sensitive regimes without meaningful inference overhead.
keywords: industrial control systems (ICS);anomaly detection;graph autoencoder;graph neural networks (GNN);explainable AI (XAI);SHAP;SCADA;PLC

title: GaP-Aug: Gamma Patch-Wise Correction Augmentation Method for Respiratory Sound Classification
journal: ICASSP 2024 - 2024 IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP)
authors: A. -Y. Chang and J. -T. Tzeng and H. -Y. Chen and C. -W. Sung and C. -H. Huang and E. P. -C. Huang and C. -C. Lee
abstract: Automated auscultation analysis using electronic stethoscope has received growing interest in clinical applications. Recently, researchers showed successes by using deep learning methods to distinguish between pathological respiratory sound classes. Nevertheless, the challenge persists due to the scarcity of abnormal samples, and the distinct characteristics between low-pitched and discontinuous crackles and high-pitched and continuous wheezes. In this study, we proposed a novel augmentation method, namely gamma patch-wise correction augmentation, which directly operates on spectrograms to handle with these two challenges. We achieved state-of-the-art performances on both 60-40 official split and 80-20 cross-validation of the public ICBHI dataset, outperforming previous top-performing studies by 11.82% in sensitivity and 5.27% in ICBHI score. Furthermore, Grad-CAM analysis shows that our approach better preserves the distinctive characteristics of crackles and wheezes than SpecAug.
keywords: Data augmentation;Respiratory sound classification;Gamma correction;Mix up

title: "DAKSHAAB": An AI-Driven Chatbot for Patient Triage Using Bio-Bert
journal: 2024 International Conference on Communication, Computing, Smart Materials and Devices (ICCCSMD)
authors: A. Kashyap and M. Singhal and M. K. Vidhyalakshmi
abstract: The specialist's referral in the treatment of patients is one of the essential measures of raising the quality of the patient's care. Structures depend upon typical styles and manners which not only limit the accuracy of the matching of specialists but their scope of domain as well. This paper develops a novel solution to enhancing the process of referrals, specifically a novel chatbot powered by Bio-BERT – one of the most sophisticated models for understanding biomedical language – using other advanced NLP techniques. Our system is trained using Bio-BERT on internal data comprised of Bio and review comments of patients to ensure the chatbot considers minute details in the complaint and yearning of the patient. Certain pre- processing techniques as applied to healthcare literature biosystems and textual data greatly enhance the accuracy and relevance of specialist recommendations. Accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score are among the metrics subjected to various sets of evaluation, where a near improvement is observed with accuracy always being above 99.7% at each epoch. Such results endorse Bio-BERT's accuracy at managing the intricacies of medical language for a conceptually flawless patient specialist matching service. The disruption these technologies present in improving specialist referral systems is particularly underlined in this study.
keywords: Specialist Referrals;Chatbot;Bio-BERT;Natural Language Processing (NLP);Biomedical Text Analysis;Healthcare Text

title: Uncertainty-Aware and Explainable Feature-Level Ensembles for CT-Based Kidney Stone Detection
journal: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics, Artificial Intelligence & Networking (QPAIN)
authors: A. Khondoker and F. A. Richi and S. B. Islam and K. Tanvir and D. J. Gomes and M. Rahman
abstract: Kidney stone condition happens often and comes back again, so it is important to find stones early with Computed Tomography(CT) scans to prevent serious problems and help guide treatment.. This work proposes a CT-specific preprocessing pipeline and a feature-level ensemble model for slice-wise classification on a publicly available axial CT dataset. An image preprocessing and augmentation pipeline was used to enhance stone visibility and improve data quality before training the classification models. An ensemble model(ResNet18+DenseNet121) is constructed by concatenating 512- and 1,024-dimensional features and passing them through a multilayer perceptron fusion head. Trained with AdamW and early stopping (100 -epoch budget, best at epoch 23), the ensemble achieves a test accuracy of 0.9944, precision of 1.0000, recall of 0.9888, F1-score of 0.9944, Matthews correlation coefficient of 0.9889, and ROC-AUC of 0.9993, outperforming all single backbones. Three-fold crossvalidation yields a mean F1-score of 0.9663 with low variance, indicating robust generalization. Monte Carlo dropout was used to estimate how confident the model is in its predictions, allowing us to identify uncertain cases and support safer, more selective clinical decision-making, while LIME, SHAP, and Grad-CAM highlight clinically plausible stone regions. These results demonstrate that a carefully designed feature-level ensemble, combined with rigorous evaluation, uncertainty estimation, and explainable AI, can deliver reliable and interpretable support for CT-based kidney stone triage.
keywords: Kidney stone detection;Computed tomography;Deep learning;Ensemble learning;Explainable artificial intelligence

title: A Data-Driven Approach to Forecasting Emergency Attendance During Easter and Labour Day Holidays
journal: 2025 IEEE CHILEAN Conference on Electrical, Electronics Engineering, Information and Communication Technologies (CHILECON)
authors: A. S. López and H. Á. Chaves and A. C. Fernández and M. D. R-Moreno
abstract: Public holidays pose a major challenge for hospital emergency departments (EDs), as they combine reduced staff availability with uncertain demand. While forecasting models are widely used for hospital planning, most evaluations rely on longterm averages, which may obscure weaknesses during short, highimpact periods. This study forecasts ED admissions and hospitalizations during Easter Week and the Labour Day holiday of 2025 in Madrid, using machine learning and statistical models enriched with exogenous variables. A nationwide blackout on April 28th was specifically addressed to avoid bias. Results show that admissions are more predictable than hos-pitalizations, with shift-level aggregation substantially improving accuracy. Exogenous variables increased performance during Easter but had limited value for Labour Day. No single model was consistently superior, underscoring the importance of contextspecific approaches.
keywords: Machine Learning;Emergency Department;Forecasting;Holiday patterns;Spanish Power Blackout;Exogenous Variables;SHAP;Boruta

title: Towards Non-Invasive Blood Group Prediction: Fingerprint Recognition with Advanced Deep Learning
journal: 2025 International Conference on Advances in Technology and Computing (ICATC)
authors: M. Vasavan and K. Luxshi and R. M. K. T. Rathanayake
abstract: Accurate and rapid identification of blood groups is critical in emergency medicine and healthcare delivery. Traditional serological methods are invasive, time-consuming, and require laboratory infrastructure. This study explores fingerprint images as a non-invasive biometric modality for blood group prediction using advanced deep learning architectures. The dataset of over 8,000 fingerprint images was preprocessed with augmentation, normalization, and noise reduction. Multiple models, including CNN variants, lightweight architectures, transformer-based models, and next-generation convolutional networks, were trained and evaluated. A weighted soft voting ensemble (0.5 EfficientNetV2-S + 0.5 MobileNetV3-Large) achieved the highest accuracy of 99.88%, outperforming individual models like MobileNetV3-Large (98.51%) and EfficientNetV2-S (97.79%). These results indicate that fingerprint-based deep learning provides a reliable, noninvasive approach for blood group prediction, with potential for deployment in mobile and point-of-care systems.
keywords: Fingerprint recognition;Blood group prediction;Deep learning;Ensemble learning;Non-invasive healthcare

title: Advances in Neuroimaging Techniques for Detection and Monitoring Intracranial Hemorrhage
journal: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Recent Advances in Computing and Systems (REACS)
authors: M. Jain
abstract: A serious medical disorder known as intracranial hemorrhage (ICH) is defined by bleeding inside the skull and frequently calls for quick diagnosis and treatment. The usual imaging method for identifying ICH is non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scans because of their quick acquisition and excellent sensitivity to acute bleeding. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs), a type of deep learning technique, have been thoroughly investigated in recent years for the purpose of detecting ICH in CT scans. To leverage both spatial and sequential information in CT scans, hybrid models combining CNNs with recurrent layers like Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks have been proposed. These models process individual slices with CNNs and capture inter-slice dependencies using LSTMs, mimicking the radiologist's approach of reviewing consecutive slices. Such architectures have shown promise in enhancing detection accuracy. The study of Intracranial Hemorrhage (ICH) detection using deep learning has significantly advanced over the years, leveraging convolutional neural networks (CNNs), transformer-based models, and hybrid architectures to improve diagnostic accuracy in CT scans. Deep learning algorithms have demonstrated near-expert performance, surpassing traditional computer-aided detection methods in speed and precision. Techniques such as transfer learning, attention mechanisms (e.g., Vision Transformers), and multi-modal fusion have enhanced feature extraction, enabling better differentiation between hemorrhage subtypes. Despite challenges like data imbalance, interpretability, and generalization across diverse datasets, recent research has focused on federated learning, explainable AI (XAI), and domain adaptation to improve clinical applicability. Integrating AI-driven ICH detection into radiology workflows has shown promising results in reducing diagnostic delays, aiding emergency triage, and improving patient outcomes in neurocritical care settings.
keywords: Bidirectional Long Short Term;Convolutional Neural Networks;Recurrent Neural Networks;Deep Learning;Intracranial Hemorrhage

title: Brain Stroke Classification Using YOLOv8
journal: 2025 26th International Arab Conference on Information Technology (ACIT)
authors: M. Elhussieni and S. Alhajj and L. Alhajj and K. Sailunaz and M. Kaya and M. K. Özdemir and J. Rokne and R. Alhajj
abstract: Brain stroke is a leading cause of mortality and long-term disability worldwide, underscoring the critical importance of rapid and accurate diagnosis for effective clinical intervention. This paper presents an automated classification approach for identifying stroke types, specifically ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, and normal brain tissues from computed tomography (CT) images using the YOLOv8 deep learning architecture. The study employs the Brain Stroke CT Dataset from the TEKNOFEST-2021 Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare Competition, which contains 6,653 anonymized and expertlabeled axial CT slices. The methodology employed in this study includes a comprehensive data preprocessing model, a fine-tuning stage using transfer learning, and performance evaluation using key metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score. Experimental results demonstrate that YOLOv8 achieves high classification accuracy across all the three categories mentioned above. This is supported by a detailed confusion matrix and visual examples of model predictions. These findings suggest that YOLOv8 can serve as a powerful tool for assisting clinicians in the rapid triage and diagnosis of patients with a brain stroke, particularly in time-sensitive scenarios. This work contributes to the growing application of artificial intelligence in medical image analysis for effective and timely decision making by offering a practical and efficient solution for stroke classification, with potential applications in both resource-limited and high-volume healthcare settings.
keywords: Brain stroke;YOLOv8;CT imaging;classification;healthcare;Artificial Intelligence;medical image analysis

title: A Cardiovascular Disease Recognition Method Based on Feature Fusion and Self-Supervised Learning
journal: 2025 22nd International Computer Conference on Wavelet Active Media Technology and Information Processing (ICCWAMTIP)
authors: X. Hu and J. Zhu and D. Li and Z. Wan
abstract: Cardiovascular diseases are closely associated with various psychological and physiological abnormalities, and their complex pathological mechanisms impose stringent requirements on diagnostic accuracy. In recent years, deep learning methods based on physiological signals have shown great potential for automated disease recognition and risk assessment. However, many existing methods rely predominantly on deep representations that often lack interpretability and fail to fully capture the intrinsic patterns embedded in physiological signals. To address these limitations, we propose a novel cardiovascular disease recognition framework that integrates multimodal feature fusion with self-supervised learning. The proposed method, termed ECG-MOEformer, jointly models 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals and clinical attributes to construct a comprehensive and interpretable disease representation. Furthermore, A contrastive self-supervised learning strategy is employed during pretraining to align cross-modal representations and enhance feature robustness using unlabeled data. Experiments conducted on the publicly available UK Biobank dataset demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves an accuracy of 0.94, a recall of 0.88, and an F1-score of 0.91, significantly outperforming several state-of-the-art baselines. Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of the hierarchical temporal encoder and multimodal fusion strategy. These results indicate that ECG-MOEformer provides a robust and interpretable solution for intelligent cardiovascular disease recognition.
keywords: Disease recognition;Physiological signals;Deep learning;Self-supervised learning;Feature fusion

title: Prediction of ICU admission for COVID-19 patients: a Machine Learning approach based on Complete Blood Count data
journal: 2021 IEEE 34th International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS)
authors: L. Famiglini and G. Bini and A. Carobene and A. Campagner and F. Cabitza
abstract: In this article we discuss the development of prognostic Machine Learning (ML) models for COVID-19 progression: specifically, we address the task of predicting intensive care unit (ICU) admission in the next 5 days. We developed three ML models on the basis of 4995 Complete Blood Count (CBC) tests. We propose three ML models that differ in terms of interpretability: two fully interpretable models and a black-box one. We report an AUC of. 81 and. 83 for the interpretable models (the decision tree and logistic regression, respectively), and an AUC of. 88 for the black-box model (an ensemble). This shows that CBC data and ML methods can be used for cost-effective prediction of ICU admission of COVID-19 patients: in particular, as the CBC can be acquired rapidly through routine blood exams, our models could also be applied in resource-limited settings and to get fast indications at triage and daily rounds.
keywords: eXplainable AI;Machine Learning;COVID-19;Prognosis;Complete Blood Count

title: Clinical vs. Ultrasound for PCOS Detection: A Calibrated, Leakage-Safe, Real-Time Benchmark
journal: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
authors: M. A. Uddin Siyam and S. Alam Shorna and S. M. Rizvi and F. Anam Jibon and R. Akter and R. Bhuiyan
abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is commonly diagnosed through clinical, biochemical, and ultrasound indicators, yet most AI studies isolate one modality. This work presents a unified, leakage-safe comparison between two pipelines: a soft-voting ensemble (XGBoost+LightGBM+CatBoost) trained on structured data and a ConvNeXt-Small model trained on high-resolution ultrasound images. Using public datasets (541 clinical records, 3,200 images), both are evaluated under identical 5-fold out-of-fold settings with explicit calibration. The clinical ensemble substantially outperforms the image model (AUROC 0.976 vs. 0.814; Brier 0.056 vs. 0.176). At stringent operating constraints (sensitivity/specificity ≥0.85), only the clinical model meets the target. Both achieve real-time inference (clinical: 57 ms, image: 30 ms), with the clinical ensemble offering 2.6× higher batch throughput. Decision-curve analysis and explainability tools show complementary insights. Results suggest structured features currently hold a stronger predictive signal, while ultrasound provides visual support and rapid triage capability.
keywords: PCOS;Machine Learning;Ensemble Methods;Calibration;ConvNeXt;Decision Support

title: Explainable AI Cloud Security Framework with Automating SIEM Event Management
journal: 2026 6th International Conference on Sensors and Information Technology (ICSI)
authors: Y. Liu and H. Bai and J. Coffman and W. Ma
abstract: We study how AI-driven security automation can be systematically designed for resource-constrained cloud environments such as small business and medical environments in remote areas. Existing SIEM deployments often rely on loosely coupled integrations and manual triage workflows, lacking formalized closed-loop orchestration under latency and operational constraints. We propose a deployment-aware AI security orchestration framework that formalizes the trigger chain (event → triage → action → visualization → refinement) as a latency-aware closedloop workflow. Unlike conventional engineering integrations, our approach treats operability and inference latency as first-class design objectives. Our novelty lies in the formalization of an operationally constrained closed-loop orchestration and its measurable system-level metrics, rather than the specific vendor tools used The framework introduces three contributions. First, a system-level orchestration model that bridges AI inference with cloud deployment through explicit workflow formalization under operational constraints Second, a deployment-aware model training and selection strategy that structures event attributes into categorical, contextual, and behavioral feature groups and frames model choice as a multi-criteria decision problem balancing predictive accuracy, inference latency, computational overhead, and interpretability. Model outputs are mapped into operational risk tiers via a defined transformation function, enabling direct integration with automated response policies. Thirdly, a quantitative operational evaluation framework defining end-to-end workflow latency and reduction of manual intervention as measurable system metrics. The experiments on a large-scale labeled security event dataset demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces manual intervention and improves response efficiency while maintaining high classification precision. In this work refers both to the repeatable deployment of the cloud security pipeline and to the reproducibility of experimental results within the deployed environment. All components, datasets, and procedures are documented; all experimental artifacts are publicly released to ensure reproducible deployment and transparent validation. It provides a complete Project reproduction repository (including data, attack examples, experiment results, Analysis charts, dashboard demo), an available for local-run dashboard program code, and a steps operation manual for reproduce and verification. (Link: weijunma/AI-Driven-Cloud-Security-Framework-SMEHealthcare at V1.1.0 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17605067).
keywords: adaptive security policies;AI-driven security;cloud computing security;explainable AI;machine learning;deep neural network;SIEM automation;Threat detection Security and Privacy;Social and Professional Topics;Automation

title: An Enhanced Random Forest Model for Predicting Serum Creatinine in Chronic Kidney Disease
journal: 2025 28th International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
authors: M. M. R. Akib and H. Rahaman and A. D. Niloy
abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is frequently detected late, constraining therapeutic options. This paper develops an interpretable, data-integrated regression framework for estimating serum creatinine (SCr) from routinely collected clinical variables to support earlier assessment in laboratory-constrained settings. Two public datasets (UCI CKD and Kaggle CKD) were merged and harmonized; a hybrid imputation strategy handled missingness while preserving distributional properties across sources. The pipeline applied chi-square feature screening, standardized preprocessing, and hyperparameter tuning via 5-fold crossvalidation on the training partition $(80 \%)$, with performance reported on an untouched 20 % test set using mean squared error (MSE), root MSE (RMSE), and $R^{2}$. We compared a parsimonious linear baseline (OLS), two tree-based nonparametric regressors (Random Forest, XGBoost), and a probabilistic neural approach (Bayesian neural network with Monte Carlo dropout). On the held-out test data, the Random Forest regressor achieved the best fit ($\mathbf{M S E}=0.0158, \boldsymbol{R M S E}=0.126, \mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=0.98$), outperforming XGBoost ($\text{MSE}=0.0388, \text{RMSE}=0.197, R^{2}=0.95$) and the Bayesian neural network ($\text{MSE}=0.513, \text{RMSE}=0.716$, $R^{2}=0.38$); OLS underperformed ($\mathbf{M S E}=2.22, R^{2}=-2.67$). SHAP and partial-dependence analyses consistently highlighted hemoglobin, systolic blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, and age as dominant contributors, aligning with established clinical knowledge. By coupling high predictive fidelity with transparent, model-agnostic explanations, the proposed approach can enable pragmatic triage and longitudinal monitoring without expanding test panels. Future work will assess external validity on larger, prospective cohorts and examine transportability across care sites.
keywords: Bayesian neural network (BNN);chronic kidney disease (CKD);eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost);interpretable machine learning;random forest;serum creatinine

title: Interpretable Summaries of Black Box Incident Triaging with Subgroup Discovery
journal: 2021 IEEE 8th International Conference on Data Science and Advanced Analytics (DSAA)
authors: Y. Remil and A. Bendimerad and M. Plantevit and C. Robardet and M. Kaytoue
abstract: The need of predictive maintenance comes with an increasing number of incidents reported by monitoring systems and equipment/software users. In the front line, on-call engineers (OCEs) have to quickly assess the degree of severity of an incident and decide which service to contact for corrective actions. To automate these decisions, several predictive models have been proposed, but the most efficient models are opaque (say, black box), strongly limiting their adoption. In this paper, we propose an efficient black box model based on 170K incidents reported to our company over the last 7 years and emphasize on the need of automating triage when incidents are massively reported on thousands of servers running our product, an ERP. Recent developments in eXplainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) help in providing global explanations to the model, but also, and most importantly, with local explanations for each model prediction/outcome. Sadly, providing a human with an explanation for each outcome is not conceivable when dealing with an important number of daily predictions. To address this problem, we propose an original data-mining method rooted in Subgroup Discovery, a pattern mining technique with the natural ability to group objects that share similar explanations of their black box predictions and provide a description for each group. We evaluate this approach and present our preliminary results which give us good hope towards an effective OCE's adoption. We believe that this approach provides a new way to address the problem of model agnostic outcome explanation.
keywords: Maintenance;Incident Triage;Software Engineering;Explainable AI;Subgroup Discovery;Data Mining

title: XFMP: A Benchmark for Explainable Fine-Grained Abnormal Behavior Recognition on Medical Personal Protective Equipment
journal: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
authors: J. Liu and J. Niu and W. Li and X. Li and B. He and H. Zhou and Y. Liu and D. Li and B. Wang and W. Zhang
abstract: The proper use of medical personal protective equipment (MPPE) is critical for frontline healthcare workers (HCWs) to handle highly contagious diseases. Due to the complexity of PPE donning and doffing protocols, public health organizations typically recommend having trained observers monitor the entire PPE donning and doffing process, preventing self-contamination and transmission. However, the high costs of manual monitoring impede the implementation of this practice, which makes AI-assisted PPE monitoring highly valuable. Some studies have applied computer vision techniques to PPE monitoring, but they have only focused on limited integrity checks at donning completion, which is unable to provide real-time warnings for abnormal actions during the doffing process. Furthermore, model practicality and user-friendliness are constrained by the lack of explainability. To address this, we propose an explainable and fine-grained dataset for MPPE doffing monitoring called the XFMP dataset. The dataset contains 3596 expert-annotated samples over three sub-tasks: doffing stage classification (DSC), abnormal action recognition (AAR), and critical region localization (CRL). Accordingly, we introduce multi-dimensional evaluation metrics for XFMP and a multitask human behavior semantic attention network (MHBSAN). Experiments demonstrate that MHBSAN outperforms alternative approaches, achieving 0.968/0.855 accuracy for stage/action classification and 0.791 Top-1 Loc@0.5 for CRL sub-task. Moreover, it demonstrates exceptional adaptability across different healthcare environments. Ablation studies and case analyses further validate the contributions and efficacy of the proposed model regarding classification and explainability.
keywords: Abnormal behavior recognition;medical personal protective equipment;explainable artificial intelligence;multitask learning

title: SA-UCA-CNN: A Single-Model Framework for Patient-Level CXR Triage with Style Alignment and Uncertainty Calibration
journal: 2025 IEEE 8th International Conference on Information Systems and Computer Aided Education (ICISCAE)
authors: W. Zhao and M. N. H. Bin Ibrahim
abstract: We address report delays and priority mismatch during patient surges. We propose SA-UCA-CNN, a deployable, single-model framework for patient-level chest X-ray (CXR) triage. The method embeds a lightweight ViT-Adapter at each stage of a single CNN and fuses it with SAAF. This adds long-range and multi-scale representations with minimal overhead. During training, a Style-Consistency GAN performs crosshospital style alignment and long-tail augmentation. At inference, we keep only the CNN+Adapter path. We apply temperature scaling, selective prediction, and Monte-Carlo (MC) dropout. They map multi-label probabilities to three triage levels—urgent, high-priority, and routine—and provide calibrated uncertainty and Grad-CAM explanations. We train and internally validate on NIH ChestX-ray14. On CheXpert and MIMIC-CXR, the model reaches area under the receiver operating characteristic (AUROC)=0.900 and area under the precision-recall curve (AUPRC)=0.540, outperforming a pure CNN (0.820/0.410). The out-of-domain drop shrinks to $\triangle \text{AUROC}=-0.018$ with expected calibration error $(E C E)=0.036$. Inference latency is 22.5 ms. Ablations show that S3+S4 with medium-intensity style augmentation offers the best performance-cost trade-off. $S2 + S3 + S4$ performs slightly better but is slower. A GAN-only scheme supports ultra-low latency. An Adapter-only variant markedly improves calibration. Overall, the framework improves external generalization, long-tail recall, and risk consistency without adding deployment complexity. It provides an auditable and reproducible engineering path for clinical CXR triage.
keywords: Chest X-ray (CXR);patient-level triage;ViTAdapter;generative style alignment;uncertainty calibration;selective prediction;external generalization;long-tail recall

title: Dense Pixel-Labeling For Reverse-Transfer And Diagnostic Learning On Lung Ultrasound For Covid-19 And Pneumonia Detection
journal: 2021 IEEE 18th International Symposium on Biomedical Imaging (ISBI)
authors: G. R. Gare and A. Schoenling and V. Philip and H. V. Tran and B. P. deBoisblanc and R. L. Rodriguez and J. M. Galeotti
abstract: We propose using a pre-trained segmentation model to perform diagnostic classification in order to achieve better generalization and interpretability, terming the technique reverse-transfer learning. We present an architecture to convert segmentation models to classification models. We compare and contrast dense vs sparse segmentation labeling and study its impact on diagnostic classification. We compare the performance of U-Net trained with dense and sparse labels to segment A-lines, B-lines, and Pleural lines on a custom dataset of lung ultrasound scans from 4 patients. Our experiments show that dense labels help reduce false positive detection. We study the classification capability of the dense and sparse trained U-Net and contrast it with a non-pretrained U-Net, to detect and differentiate COVID-19 and Pneumonia on a large ultrasound dataset of about 40k curvilinear and linear probe images. Our segmentation-based models perform better classification when using pretrained segmentation weights, with the dense-label pretrained U-Net performing the best.
keywords: Deep Learning;Dense Semantic Segmentation;Diagnostic Classification;Ultrasound Lung Scans;COVID-19 Detection

title: Explainable Temporal Attention for Anomaly Detection in Medical Time-Series Data
authors: S. Benkrid and L. Hamdad and K. A. Habouche
abstract: The effective interpretation of medical time-series data remains a significant challenge in AI diagnostics, as temporal patterns critical for diagnosis are often obscured in conventional “black-box” models. This paper presents MedAttnAID, an explainable temporal attention framework designed for unsupervised anomaly detection in sensor-generated medical time-series data. Our approach integrates a bidirectional LSTM autoencoder with interpretable attention mechanisms that highlight diagnostically relevant temporal segments, complemented by a novel Clinical Pattern Loss (CPLoss) function that preserves clinically significant temporal patterns during reconstruction. We validate the framework on thermal time-series data from wearable breast cancer monitoring devices, achieving $85.1 \% ~\mathrm{F} 1$ score and 95 % breast-level localization accuracy while producing interpretable attention heatmaps that align with clinical expectations. The framework's modular architecture addresses fundamental challenges common to sensor-based medical monitoring-limited labeled pathological data, clinical interpretability requirements, and detection of subtle anomalies in complex temporal pat-terns-making it broadly applicable to diverse sensing modalities including ECG, EEG, and continuous physiological monitoring systems.
keywords: Intelligent Environments;Smart Healthcare;Time-Series Analysis;Unsupervised Anomaly Detection;Explainable AI (XAI);LSTM;Temporal Attention

title: Sustainable AI for Medical Imaging: A Federated, Edge-based Approach to Chest X-ray Triage
journal: 2025 International Conference on Modern Sustainable Systems (CMSS)
authors: R. Ranganathan and A. Annamalai and S. Ruban and S. Mythili and B. Shuriya and V. Balajishanmugam
abstract: Introduction In recent years, the emerging technology of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has made huge strides in its application to medical diagnostics, achieving outstanding accuracy and efficiency. However, the sustainability of such applications has not been well-investigated. Such conventional deep learning models in healthcare require heavy computation, internet access and central available data storage, which raise an issue regarding energy consumption, fairness and sustainability. In this paper, we explore a green solution for triaging chest X-rays towards the detection of pneumonia using AI, by comparing a traditional cloud-based inference solution based on ResNet50 to a MobileNetV2 model compressed via federated learning and deployed on edge-devices. We then evaluated the two systems across diagnostic performance, energy consumption, demographic fairness, inference latency, and transparency on a subset of the NIH ChestX-ray14 dataset. The results suggest that the sustainable system retained a similar level of accuracy while significantly reduced inference energy (up to >80%), improving fairness measures and enabling explainability through SHAP-based visualization. Our results show that AI systems designed with sustainability in mind can deliver clinically effective and environmentally responsible systems, ideally suited to scalable and equitable deployment across diverse healthcare contexts.
keywords: Artificial Intelligence;medical diagnostics;chest X-rays and visualization

title: AI-Enhanced Telehealth Platforms: A Comprehensive Analysis of Automated Triage and Personalized Care Systems
authors: S. K. Lagisetty and P. Devarajulu and A. K. Moka
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of artificial intelligence (AI) integration in telehealth platforms, focusing on automated triage systems and personalized care recommendations. We examine how AI technologies are revolutionizing virtual healthcare delivery through improved patient assessment, risk stratification, and customized treatment planning. Through critical analysis of technical implementations and case studies, we evaluate both the benefits and limitations of current AI-driven solutions. Our findings reveal significant improvements in operational efficiency and patient outcomes, while highlighting persistent challenges in data privacy, interoperability, and model interpretability. We conclude with evidence-based recommendations for future development and implementation of AI in telehealth systems.
keywords: AI-Enhanced Telehealth;Automated Triage Systems;Personalized Care;Virtual Healthcare Delivery

title: Blood Alcohol Concentration Screening at Emergency Room: Designing a Classification Model Using Machine Learning
journal: 2023 14th International Conference on Information & Communication Technology and System (ICTS)
authors: N. P. Martono and S. Kuramaru and Y. Igarashi and S. Yokobori and H. Ohwada
abstract: Conventional alcohol screening methods in the ER are susceptible to errors, potentially compromising patient safety and treatment efficacy. Thus, the study aimed to develop an improved classification model utilizing blood gas data and machine learning techniques. Patient data collected from the ER formed the dataset, with blood gas data available for each patient. Five distinct machine learning algorithms—K-nearest neighbor, logistic regression, random forest, LightGBM, and support vector machine (SVM)—were employed to construct the classification model. Model performance evaluation encompassed sensitivity, specificity, and mean absolute error metrics. To contend with challenges arising from intricate feature dimensions and skewed data distribution, the study incorporated feature selection techniques like the Filter and Wrapped Methods. Additionally, the SMOTEENN sampling approach was adopted to address data imbalance. Of the evaluated algorithms, the LightGBM model notably excelled, boasting an accuracy rate of 0.908 and an F-score of 0.617. This underscores the efficacy of utilizing blood gas analysis data for BAC prediction. The developed classification model holds potential for enhancing the precision and expediency of alcohol screening procedures within ER settings, enabling more informed medical decisions by healthcare providers.
keywords: blood alcohol;machine learning;classification model;emergency room

title: Multi-modal Machine Learning for CCTA Referral Decision: Integrating Opportunistic Coronary Calcium Screening from LDCT with Clinical Data
journal: 2025 Second International Conference on Artificial Intelligence for Medicine, Health and Care (AIxMHC)
authors: K. -T. Wu and H. -R. Liu and W. -H. Yin and S. -Y. Huang and J. -S. Hong and G. -Y. Li and C. -F. Lu and Y. -H. Tzeng and Y. -T. Wu
abstract: Lung cancer screening CT presents an unparalleled opportunity for opportunistic cardiovascular risk assessment via coronary artery calcification (CAC), yet determining when asymptomatic individuals warrant coronary CT angiography (CCTA) remains challenging. We developed and validated a multi-modal machine learning framework that integrates CAC metrics automatically derived from screening CT with comprehensive health check data to guide CCTA referral decisions in 476 asymptomatic adults. Using a validated nnU-Net model for CAC segmentation and training nine algorithms plus ensemble methods on thirty-four clinical variables and three imaging metrics, we achieved a best AUC of 0.911 with Random Forest and a top accuracy of 0.896 with a Multi-Layer Perceptron on an independent test cohort. Ablation experiments demonstrated the supremacy of imaging-only ensembles (AUC = 0.966, accuracy = 0.917) for the imaging-derived CAD-RADS ≥ 3 end point, whereas SHAP analysis confirmed CAC scores as the dominant predictors. This framework enables actionable CCTA triage from lung cancer screening CT combined with routine health data, adding significant cardiovascular risk stratification value to existing screening paradigms without additional scans or cost.
keywords: Coronary artery calcification;low-dose computed tomography;machine learning;coronary CT angiography;opportunistic screening;multi-modal integration

title: Towards Balancing Preference and Performance through Adaptive Personalized Explainability
journal: 2024 19th ACM/IEEE International Conference on Human-Robot Interaction (HRI)
authors: A. Silva and P. Tambwekar and M. Schrum and M. Gombolay
abstract: As robots and digital assistants are deployed in the real world, these agents must be able to communicate their decision-making criteria to build trust, improve human-robot teaming, and enable collaboration. While the field of explainable artificial intelligence (xAI) has made great strides to enable such communication, these advances often assume that one xAI approach is ideally suited to each problem (e.g., decision trees to explain how to triage patients in an emergency or feature-importance maps to explain radiology reports). This fails to recognize that users have diverse experiences or preferences for interaction modalities. In this work, we present two user-studies set in a simulated autonomous vehicle (AV) domain. We investigate (1) population-level preferences for xAI and (2) personalization strategies for providing robot explanations. We find significant differences between xAI modes (language explanations, feature-importance maps, and decision trees) in both preference (p < 0.01) and performance (p < 0.05). We also observe that a participant’s preferences do not always align with their performance, motivating our development of an adaptive personalization strategy to balance the two. We show that this strategy yields significant performance gains (p < 0.05), and we conclude with a discussion of our findings and implications for xAI in human-robot interactions.CCS CONCEPTS• Human-centered computing → Human computer interaction (HCI); • Computing methodologies → Artificial intelligence.
keywords: Explainability;Personalization;User Studies

title: Visual Acuity Classification Using Ensemble Machine Learning Algorithms: With Explainable Approach
journal: 2023 International Conference on Information and Communication Technology for Development for Africa (ICT4DA)
authors: R. Y. Ephrem and A. M. Yibre
abstract: Visual acuity is an important aspect of overall health, and early detection of visual problems can prevent long-term complications. This study explores the use of ensemble machine learning algorithms to predict visual acuity categories before they happen. We compare the performance of different types of ensemble algorithms, AdaBoost, XGBoost, Gradient Boosting, Stacking and Bagging Classification accuracy is 0.99, 0.98, 0.99, 0.98 and 0.99 respectively. Parameter optimization is also used to find the best set of hyper-parameters for a model that will help it perform optimally. In addition, we investigate the impact of various attributes, including living conditions, age, gender, and source of drinking water, on visual acuity classification. We employed SHAP for model interpretation and explanation. Our results revealed that these factors can indeed be risk factors for blindness or visual impairment, and that incorporating them into the prediction model can improve accuracy and early detection. Our research offers for predicting and preventing visual acuity categories. By identifying individuals at risk, we can implement timely interventions and treatments, consequently improving the quality of life for those affected.
keywords: visual acuity;eye disease;ensemble machine learning;XGBoost;explainable machine learning

title: Pneumonia Detection Using a Hybrid CNN and Swin Transformer Architecture
journal: 2026 Fourth International Conference on Augmented Intelligence and Sustainable Systems (ICAISS)
authors: S. B. P and K. S. Reddy and S. H. Vardhan and P. P. Sai and P. R. Reddy
abstract: Pneumonia remains a serious respiratory infection for which early identification can improve clinical outcomes. Yet, reading chest radiographs is time-consuming and can vary across observers, especially where experienced radiologists are scarce. This work introduces an automated pneumonia screening model that merges a ResNet-50 convolutional feature extractor (for local patterns) with a Swin Transformer component (for global context reasoning). We evaluate the approach on the Kaggle Chest X-ray Pneumonia dataset using 5,216 training images and 624 test images, obtaining 83.65 % accuracy and 92.05 % recall, which indicates strong sensitivity for triage-oriented use. For interpretability and practical deployment, Grad-CAM heatmaps are generated and a lightweight web interface is provided. Key implementation choices and hyperparameters are documented to support reproducibility and further development.
keywords: Pneumonia detection;chest X-ray;deep learning;ResNet-50;Swin Transformer;Grad-CAM;explainable AI

title: Temporal Decomposition and Attention-Based Deep Learning for Magnetocardiography Signal Denoising
journal: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
authors: Y. Jia and H. Pei and K. Ma and Y. Qi and D. Xu and J. Pang and Y. Chen and Y. Cui and M. Xiang
abstract: This article proposes a temporal decomposition and attention-based denoising network (TADNet) for magnetocardiography (MCG) signal denoising. The raw time-series data are decomposed into trend and seasonal components. The trend component is modeled using a multilayer perceptron (MLP) to capture the trend of the data. For seasonal components, a multilayer convolutional neural network (CNN) is employed to perform segmentation and extract local temporal features. These fine-grained features are processed by a Transformer-based self-attention mechanism to capture long-range temporal dependencies. Finally, deconvolution operations are applied to reconstruct the signal, achieving effective noise reduction for MCG data. This article conducts in-depth studies on the effects of time, wavelet, and Fourier-style attention on model performance, enhancing the interpretability of the model. Extensive experiments on clinical MCG data under various noise conditions demonstrate that the TADNet outperforms traditional algorithms, proving its effectiveness and robustness. The research results indicate that the TADNet provides a highly efficient and accurate solution for MCG signal denoising.
keywords: Attention mechanisms;Fourier attention;magnetocardiography (MCG);patch segmentation;signal denoising

title: LGAF-Net: A Local-Global Attention Fusion Network for Efficient Medical Image Classification
journal: 2025 5th International Conference on Digital Futures and Transformative Technologies (ICoDT2)
authors: J. Abbas and D. B. Soomro and M. Buriro and M. Y. Khan and S. Abbas and M. Afzal
abstract: Medical image analysis is critical for early screening, triage, and treatment planning. However, automated methods face challenges due to small lesion sizes, heterogeneous acquisitions, and the trade-off between local spatial precision and global contextual reasoning.
